name: TX-14
label: Likely R

model.rationale: Weber holds a heavily Republican seat with a dominant fundraising edge and no serious outside opposition, while Bartie has raised almost nothing and is out of cash. Markets price Weber around 95%, consistent with a likely-but-not-impossible Democratic upset.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Weber would be the first sign the race is competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Randy Weber seeks another term in a southeast Texas district that leans about twelve points Republican at the baseline. He is running as the incumbent with roughly $920,000 on hand, while Democrat Thurman Bartie has raised under $30,000 and reports negative cash. No outside groups are spending against Weber, and no public polls cover the race.

Prediction markets give Weber about a 95% chance of winning. With no expert ratings or polling to lean on, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap, all of which point to a comfortable Weber win with modest residual uncertainty.
